selected_subject.texas_tie: Founder and CEO moving Auger's headquarters and customer-facing expansion to North Dallas

selected_decision.what_happened: Dave Clark chose to move Auger's headquarters from the Seattle area to Dallas, placing customer-facing teams and part of the science organization in Dallas while retaining and expanding the technical operation in Bellevue.
selected_decision.owner_evidence: D Magazine's original interview records Clark explaining why he and co-founder Leigh Anne Clark chose Dallas for the go-to-market and customer phase. GeekWire separately identifies him as Auger's co-founder and CEO, calls the relocation his decision, and reports his plan to retain and expand the Bellevue engineering office.
selected_decision.alternative_available: Keep the headquarters, customer management, and go-to-market buildout with the established technical organization in the Seattle area. Clark instead chose a two-city structure that puts the headquarters and customer-facing expansion in Dallas while preserving the Bellevue engineering base.
selected_decision.ai_nexus: Auger describes its product as an autonomous operating system for supply chains. D Magazine reports that the software connects fragmented enterprise systems so AI can make and execute routine inventory, vendor, and shipping decisions while people handle more complicated problems.
selected_decision.texas_consequence: North Dallas becomes the corporate headquarters and the base for customer-facing, go-to-market, supply-chain, solutions, and some science roles. D Magazine reported an opening team of about a dozen with a plan to grow to roughly 30 by the end of 2026, while GeekWire reported about 15 people and a plan to add another 20 to 30 by the middle of 2027.
selected_decision.next_check: At the end of 2026, verify whether the Dallas office reaches roughly 30 employees, whether Auger's public company profiles identify Dallas as headquarters, and whether hiring actually spans customer-facing and science roles. By the middle of 2027, compare the separate GeekWire hiring target with actual Dallas staffing.

Auger's software integrates AI into supply-chain automation.

corroborating_sources.title: Auger company page and Dallas update
claims_supported: Auger opened a Dallas office for customer-facing teams and part of its science organization.
The company said its technical organization remains in the Seattle area.
The company page describes Auger as an autonomous operating system for supply-chain operations.
The fetched profile metadata still listed Bellevue as headquarters.

evidence_for: The two-city plan assigns different work to different labor markets instead of treating the move as a symbolic headquarters swap.
Dallas has a named office, identified role families, two independently reported staffing milestones, and no reported state or local incentive dependency.
Bellevue remains the large technical base, reducing the risk of discarding the engineering organization already built there.
evidence_against: The staffing plan is still a forecast, and the two independent reports describe different starting counts and growth horizons.
Auger's fetched LinkedIn profile metadata still listed Bellevue as headquarters even though the company posted about the Dallas opening and linked both relocation stories.
The fetched sources do not yet show whether splitting customer, science, and technical teams across two cities improves execution or recreates the coordination cost Auger says its product removes.
analysis.structural_read: This is less a simple headquarters relocation than a division of labor. Clark is concentrating customer access and applied supply-chain talent in Dallas while keeping the engineering system in Bellevue. The decision tests whether an AI company can organize around two distinct labor markets without creating a new internal coordination layer.
analysis.forward_implication: If the Dallas hiring and role split become real, North Texas gains an operating center for applied supply-chain AI rather than a mailing address. If the public headquarters label, staffing, and science roles do not converge, the move will have outrun the organization behind it.
analysis.conflict_screen_note: No payment, sponsorship, employment, customer, investor, or editorial relationship was supplied or identified. Company product claims are attributed and are not treated as measured performance.

gate_evidence.named_subject: Auger's current About page and both independent interviews identify Dave Clark as founder and CEO.
gate_evidence.recent_decision: The relocation was reported and explained on August 10th and August 12th, 2026, inside the 60-day window.
gate_evidence.decision_owner: Clark gave two direct interviews explaining the chosen two-city structure and the talent logic behind it.
gate_evidence.texas_ai_consequence: Dallas becomes the headquarters and base for customer-facing and some science roles at an applied supply-chain AI company, with measurable staffing targets.
gate_evidence.primary_source: D Magazine's complete original interview with the decision owner was fetched in this run.
gate_evidence.independent_corroboration: GeekWire's separate original interview and reporting were fetched and independently corroborate the relocation, staffing, and retained Bellevue operation.
gate_evidence.position_or_accountability_read: The analysis tests the stated division of labor against actual staffing, public headquarters metadata, and cross-office execution.
gate_evidence.not_recent_repeat: History scan lists only Joydeep Biswas, Noah Schochet, and Leann Kidd; Clark and this decision have not been selected in a prior run.
gate_evidence.conflict_clear: No editorial relationship or conflict was identified, and company product claims remain attributed.
gate_evidence.political_neutrality: The post covers a private business decision and omits the separate political claims in the GeekWire interview.

challenge_pass: Clark's current founder and CEO role was checked against Auger's current About page and both independent interviews.
The decision is a completed headquarters relocation with an open Dallas office, not only an aspiration.
The August 10th date is the public disclosure date supported by the first original report, not an invented internal deliberation date.
Clark's ownership is supported by his direct explanation of the chosen operating split and by GeekWire's separate interview.
The AI nexus is Auger's operating product, not a generic claim that every supply-chain software company is an AI company.
The alternative is bounded to keeping the headquarters and commercial buildout with the established Seattle-area technical operation.
The two independent outlets conducted separate interviews and are not company releases or syndicated copies.
The fetched company profile's Bellevue headquarters metadata is preserved as a gap rather than ignored.
The differing Dallas staffing baselines and horizons are both disclosed rather than blended into one unsupported promise.
The selected subject and decision clear the 21-day cooldown and permanent subject-decision history block.
Political commentary in the GeekWire interview is excluded because it is not necessary to assess the business execution choice.
